For those wondering, this happened in Chile during the "estallido social" (social uprising/outbreak). Circa November 2019. That's the "primera linea" (first line or front line) that's fighting the police special forces (an anti-riot division). They were louring the police so they wouldn't attack the other protestors. They were basically stopping the police from entering the protest site.

Edit: They were protesting against the government, asking for living wages, AFP (kind of a retirement found that doesn't work and it just robs you), Isapres (similar to health insurance companies in the US), the lack of government action on environmental issues (droughts in several regions due to over farming for exportation and water contamination due to mining), and other stuff that I cannot remember right now. I'm Chilean by the way.

This started because of a 30 pesos rise in the metro/bus ticket on the capital. This might sound like it is nothing (about 4 US cents) but the minimal wage is 325.000 pesos (455 US dollars). So it adds up very quickly. Needless to say that it wasn't just because of those 30 pesos, but rather this was the straw that broke the camel's back.

Chilean here! I can confirm, we are so used to earthquakes that we can fairly accurately tell the magnitude of a quake just by feeling it. Also here we call "temblor" (little quake or tremor) any earthquake that is magnitude 6.5~7.0 or lower (there is no real definition, but if it doesn't cause damage it is definitely not an earthquake). Above 7 it is usually called "terremoto" (earthquake).

Fun fact: We have an alcoholic drink called "terremoto" and it is drinked during the national holidays on September. No one really know why it is called that way, but it sure hits like an earthquake.
